q: 1. Two hill tops A and B 20 km apart are intervened by a third top C. If the top most contour of the three hill tops are of the same value, state whether the line of sight AB
options: passes below the hill top C
passes below the hill top C
explain: Due to the earth's curvature, the line of sight between two points at the same elevation will pass below the actual ground level of an intervening point of that same elevation.

q: 2. The best method of interpolation of contours, is by
explain: Interpolation by arithmetical calculation (computation) is the most accurate method, though it is slower than estimation or graphical methods.

q: 3. For preparation of contour plan for a route survey
options: method of trace contour is used
method of cross profile is used
indirect method of contouring is used
explain: In route surveys for roads or railways, cross-sections (profiles) are taken at regular intervals along the centerline to determine the topography of the narrow strip.

q: 4. Accuracy of elevation of various points obtained from contour map is limited to
explain: The standard acceptable error in interpolated elevations from a contour map is generally taken as half of the contour interval.

q: 5. The tacheometric method of contouring is particularly suitable .............
options: when a contoured map of hill is required
when the area is not very extensive
in surfaces of roads or railways
explain: Tacheometry is ideal for hilly terrain where chaining is difficult or impossible due to steep slopes and obstacles.

q: 6. The space of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually .............
explain: In rugged or hilly terrain, cross-sections are typically spaced every 20m to capture significant changes in topography without excessive labor.

q: 7. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation if contours .............
explain: Arithmetical calculation is the most accurate method for interpolation, as it assumes a uniform slope between points and calculates the exact position of the contour line.

q: 8. The vertical distance between any two consecutive contours is called .............
explain: Contour Interval is the constant vertical distance between successive contour lines.

q: 9. The horizontal distance between any two consecutive contours is called .............
explain: Horizontal Equivalent is the distance between two contour lines measured on a map, which varies according to the steepness of the slope.

q: 10. When several contours coincide, it indicates .............
explain: Contours coincide to form a single line only in the case of a vertical cliff.
